One script starts a highway, four beacon validators, five shard validators and a full node on your machine.
Zephyrium is a layer-1 chain where privacy is the default for transfers.

Transfers of ZEP and tokens Swaps on pDEX Staking Sender Hidden in a ring of 8 Hidden in a ring of 8 Public Receiver One-time address One-time address Public Amount Hidden Public Public Which token Hidden for tokens in confidential-asset mode Public ZEP only Three mechanisms do the work: Ring signatures. A spend is signed by a ring of eight keys. One is the real spender; seven are decoys taken from the chain. One-time addresses. Every payment lands on a fresh address derived for that payment, so two payments to the same person look unrelated. Hidden amounts. Amounts are commitments. A range proof shows the amount is valid and that inputs equal outputs, without revealing the number.

Shards process transactions, token transfers and swaps. The devnet runs one shard. The beacon chain coordinates the shards: it records who the validators are, confirms shard blocks and carries messages between shards. Committees of validators sign blocks. A block is final when more than two thirds of the committee sign it. The highway is a relay that every node connects to. It introduces nodes to each other and forwards their messages. Node types explains who runs each part.

These are known and on the roadmap: Small rings with uniform decoys. Eight members, chosen without regard to coin age, is weaker than a larger, age-aware ring. Swap amounts are public. pDEX hides who trades, not how much or which pair. The highway is a single relay. It can see which address a transaction came from, and the chain stops if it is down. Fixed committee seats. On the devnet, 5 of 7 shard seats and all 4 beacon seats are held by fixed validators. Wallets share a viewing key with their node. A wallet registers a viewing key with the node it uses so the node can find its coins. No slashing penalty. A validator that misbehaves loses its seat and gets its stake back.
A devnet is a complete private network on one machine: a highway, 4 beacon validators, 5 shard validators and a full node. It produces a block about every 10 seconds.
Go 1.24 or newer, python3, curl macOS or Linux. Only macOS on Apple Silicon has been tested. Free ports: 9330, 9334-9344, 9350-9354, 9434-9454

Validator and treasury keys live in secrets/secrets.json, which is git-ignored. On a new machine: mkdir -p secrets && cd secrets GO111MODULE=on GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go run -ldflags=-checklinkname=0 ../utility/genzephyriumkeys # writes keylist.json, keylist-v2.json and secrets.json into this folder cp keylist.json keylist-v2.json ../config/local/ cd .. GO111MODULE=on GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go run -ldflags=-checklinkname=0 ./utility/gengenesis gengenesis adds a foundation key to secrets/secrets.json, writes the genesis allocation to config/local/init_tx.json, and sets dao_address in config/local/param.yaml to the foundation address. Nothing to paste by hand. Back up secrets/secrets.json. It is the only copy of the private keys.
GO111MODULE=on GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go build -ldflags=-checklinkname=0 -o incognito ./ The -ldflags=-checklinkname=0 flag is required with Go 1.24 or newer.
./launch_local.sh This builds the highway on first use, starts it, then starts the nodes one second apart. Logs go to logs/, chain data to data/.

python3 tests/devnet/check.py It checks block production, the genesis balance, the stake rules, the reward split after the first epoch, and a DEX swap. It takes about 10 minutes because it waits for an epoch to end. Add --stakers to also stake two outside validators and wait until one is seated and paid (about 30 minutes; start ./start_node.sh shard0-5 and ./start_node.sh shard0-6 first). To query the chain yourself, the full node answers JSON-RPC on port 9354: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9354 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"1.0","method":"getblockchaininfo","params":[],"id":1}'

./stop_local.sh # stops only this folder's nodes and highway rm -rf data logs # optional: the next launch starts a new chain at block 1 A reset is required after changing genesis or committee settings. Do not use the inherited stop.sh; it closes every tmux session on the machine.

pDEX is an exchange that is part of the chain itself: pools and swaps are handled by the validators, with no separate contract to deploy.

Pools hold two assets and price swaps with the constant-product rule: the product of the two balances stays the same through a trade. Liquidity providers add both assets to a pool. A position is tied to a position key that the provider mints once. Swaps burn the asset being sold and pay out the asset being bought to a one-time address. Setting Devnet value Default pool fee 0.30% Highest fee a pool can have 2% Cost to mint a position key 1 ZEP

On pDEX today Who traded Hidden: the trade is signed by a ring of 8 Where the proceeds go Hidden: a one-time address Amount sold Public Token pair Public pDEX gives anonymous trades, not confidential ones. Hiding swap amounts is a research item on the roadmap.

documents.t: The devnet check creates a test token, adds a ZEP pool for it and swaps 1 ZEP: python3 tests/devnet/check.py The last line of its output reports the swap, for example DEX swap: 1 ZEP bought 1.998002 pUSDt.
The RPC methods carry the same name in lowercase: pdexv3_getState, pdexv3_txAddLiquidity and pdexv3_txTrade.
A single admin key can still change pDEX parameters such as fee rates. Removing it is the first phase of the roadmap.
An pToken is a token on Zephyrium that moves with the same privacy as ZEP: the sender hides in a ring, the receiver gets a one-time address and the amount is hidden.

Any account can create a token with a fixed supply in one transaction. The whole supply is issued to the creator. On the devnet this is the createandsendtokeninittransaction RPC method, and pWallet lists the new token once it arrives. A newly created token needs a few blocks before it can be spent.

Visible to the public? Sender No Receiver No Amount No Which token Hidden for tokens in confidential-asset mode; visible otherwise Making confidential-asset mode the rule for every token is on the roadmap.

Issuer-owned tokens with a public registry entry and an optional mintable supply. An auditor key per token, so an issuer can show activity to a regulator without showing it to everyone. Private distributions such as dividends to current holders.
The code inherited a central issuing key that can mint new tokens. It is scheduled for removal in the first phase of the roadmap.

pWallet is a Chrome extension wallet for the Zephyrium devnet. It builds private transactions in the browser, so spending keys never leave your device. Devnet only pWallet is not in the Chrome Web Store. It is loaded as an unpacked extension and connects to a devnet node. Coins on a devnet have no value.

Feature Details Send and receive ZEP Payments land on one-time addresses automatically Tokens Lists every pToken you hold and sends them pDEX Add liquidity and swap from the popup Connect to apps Web pages can request a connection, balances and transactions; each needs your approval

The wallet seed is encrypted on your device with your password. Ring signatures and range proofs are computed in the browser, then the finished transaction is sent to a node. Building a transaction takes roughly 5 to 15 seconds, and the popup has to stay open while it does.

To find your coins, the wallet registers a viewing key with the node it uses. That node can see your incoming coins; it cannot spend them. Use a node you run yourself if that matters to you. Removing this step is on the roadmap.
Transaction Minimum fee ZEP transfer 0.1 ZEP Token transaction 10 ZEP
Changes to the Zephyrium chain. Newest first.

Reward split simplified to the v3.2 release schedule: 299/979 of every block to validators, 680/979 to one foundation wallet (dao_address). The finance, DAO and satoshi addresses are gone. The foundation wallet also holds the genesis allocation; gengenesis now writes its address into param.yaml. tools/make-devnet-pack.sh builds a self-contained devnet archive with prebuilt Linux and macOS binaries for launching on another machine. Linux: the pack was launched in a Debian container.

Renamed the project to Zephyrium and the coin to ZEP. The Go module is github.com/zephyrium/zephyrium-chain. Devnet scripts read validator keys from the uncommitted secrets file; the highway creates its own network identity on start. Removed inherited scripts and files that carried upstream test keys.

ZEP minting schedule: 1,000,000,000 hard cap, 21,000,000 at genesis, 979,000,000 minted by blocks over 21 years with a 10% yearly decrease. Every block reward is split 309/330/330/10 (of 979) between validators, finance, DAO and satoshi addresses. The minting cap is counted on-chain from the first block. Genesis coins go to a newly generated treasury key (utility/gengenesis). Stake amounts come from config: 21,000 ZEP per shard validator, 210,000 ZEP beacon minimum. Devnet shard committee opened to 7 seats with 5 fixed; beacon committee closed at 4. Highway bundled under ./highway. Fixed: staked validators could not report their supported features, so they were never seated. Added tests/devnet/check.py, a regression check for the local devnet.
New committee keys generated from fresh randomness (utility/genzephyriumkeys), replacing the publicly derivable upstream test keys. Working local devnet launch.

Zephyrium is open-source software released under the MIT License. Zephyrium v1 was forked from Incognito Chain, used under the same license. We picked up that code and continue the work on it: every release after v1 is our own development. The source code and the full license notices are on GitHub.
Coming soon We are working on the roadmap and will publish it here soon. Until then, the changelog lists what has already shipped.

ZEP has a hard cap of 1,000,000,000. 71,000,000 are pre-minted at genesis for the ICO, and the remaining 929,000,000 are released over 21 years, with each year releasing 10% less than the one before. On the devnet The project devnet still runs the previous schedule (21,000,000 at genesis, 979,000,000 minted by blocks, 299 of every 979 ZEP to validators). The 71,000,000 ZEP genesis and the 299/929 split are ready in the chain repository and take effect when the devnet is reset. The split between liquidity, foundation and team, and the team cliff, are not enforced on-chain yet; see Validators and rewards.

Setting Value Hard cap 1,000,000,000 ZEP Pre-minted at genesis 71,000,000 ZEP (ICO) Released on the 21-year curve 929,000,000 ZEP Yearly decrease 10% Curve years 21 Year 1 curve release 104,313,924 ZEP Cliff, Team & Contributors 12 months

Share Of the 1B cap ZEP Release Cliff Validators 29.9% 299,000,000 21-year curve None Liquidity 21% 210,000,000 21-year curve None Foundation 21% 210,000,000 21-year curve None Team & Contributors 21% 210,000,000 21-year curve 1 year ICO 7.1% 71,000,000 Pre-minted at genesis None The ICO includes what was earlier a separate investor allocation. It is minted in the genesis block to the foundation wallet, which distributes it to buyers. Team & Contributors accrue from genesis, but nothing is liquid during the first 12 months. What they accrued in year 1 unlocks when the cliff ends, so it is counted in year 2.

Zephyrium has one network today, the local devnet, configured in config/local/. Setting Devnet value Key in param.yaml Shards 1 active_shards Block interval 10 seconds block_time Epoch length 50 beacon blocks epoch_param.number_of_block_in_epoch Shard committee 5 to 7 seats, 5 fixed committee_size Beacon committee 4 seats, 4 fixed committee_size Shard stake 21,000 ZEP staking_amount_shard Beacon stake minimum 210,000 ZEP staking_amount_beacon_min Block reward 34.834156126 ZEP per shard block basic_reward Yearly decrease 10%, for 21 years tokenomics Minted by blocks, cap 979,000,000 ZEP max_reward Reward shares 299 validators / 680 foundation tokenomics Genesis allocation 21,000,000 ZEP to the foundation wallet init_tx.json Foundation wallet Payment address of the foundation key dao_address Amounts in the config files are in the smallest unit: 1 ZEP = 1,000,000,000 units.

basic_reward is per shard block. A network with more shards or a different block interval needs a different value to mint the same yearly total. The committee members at genesis come from keylist.json: the first 4 beacon keys and the first 5 keys of shard 0. These are consensus settings. Every node must run the same values, and changing genesis or committee settings requires a new chain.

A wallet talks to a full node. Full nodes pass transactions to shard validators, who put them in blocks. Beacon validators keep the shards in step. Today a highway relays every message between them. Node Stake What it does You can run it Full node None Keeps a full copy of every chain and answers queries Yes, on the devnet Shard validator 21,000 ZEP Signs the blocks that carry transactions, tokens and swaps On the devnet, 2 open seats Beacon validator 210,000 ZEP minimum Coordinates the shards and tracks validators Not yet; the beacon committee is closed Highway None Relays messages and serves blocks to syncing nodes Devnet only; being replaced

It downloads and checks every block and answers JSON-RPC requests. It holds no validator key and never signs blocks. Run your own for independence and privacy: a wallet shares a viewing key with the node it uses, and on your own node that key stays on your machine. ./start_node.sh full_node # RPC on port 9354

A member of a shard committee. Stake exactly 21,000 ZEP, wait as a candidate, get assigned to a shard at random, sync it, then take a seat when one rotates. Seated validators earn a share of every block reward. A validator must stay online. One that misses too many signatures loses its seat at the end of the epoch. ./start_node.sh shard0-5 # one of the two spare validator nodes on the devnet

A member of the beacon committee. Only a key that is already a shard validator can apply. The stake is at least 210,000 ZEP in multiples of 21,000, and auto-restake is always on. It runs the same program as a shard validator; the beacon staking transaction is what changes its role.

A relay server. Nodes do not connect to each other directly today: each one connects to the highway. It creates its own network identity on start and needs no keys to manage. The roadmap replaces it with direct node-to-node networking before any public network.

Measured on the local devnet, which was nearly idle: Disk growth Memory at start Full node About 14 GB a year with empty blocks About 50 MB Validator About 16 GB a year with empty blocks About 50 MB Transactions add to this. Memory and processor use under real traffic have not been measured yet.
The figures are the devnet's settings in config/local/param.yaml.

Shard validator Beacon validator Stake Exactly 21,000 ZEP At least 210,000 ZEP, in multiples of 21,000 Who can apply Anyone Only a key that is already a shard validator Auto-restake Optional Always on Stake returned When the validator unstakes or loses its seat Same A staking transaction burns the stake and names the validator key. The validator then moves through four stages: Candidate: registered, waiting for the next random assignment. Syncing: assigned to a shard, downloading it. Pending: synced and waiting for a seat. Committee: seated, signing blocks and earning. Rotation happens once per epoch (50 beacon blocks on the devnet, about 8 minutes). A validator that misses too many signatures loses its seat at the end of the epoch. Today it gets its full stake back; burning part of the stake is on the roadmap.
Committee Seats Fixed seats Open to stakers Shard 0 7 5 2 Beacon 4 4 0 Fixed seats are never rotated out. A block is final when more than two thirds of the committee sign it.

Each shard block mints 34.834156126 ZEP on the devnet (one shard, 10-second blocks). The amount falls 10% each year and stops after 21 years, for a total of 979,000,000 ZEP minted by blocks. Transaction fees are added to the same pool.

Share Part of every reward Paid to Validators 299 / 979 (30.54%) Beacon and shard committees Foundation 680 / 979 (69.46%) dao_address, the foundation wallet The foundation wallet also holds the 21,000,000 ZEP genesis allocation. Over 21 years this gives validators 299,000,000 ZEP and the foundation 701,000,000 ZEP, which the foundation distributes to liquidity, team, contributors and investors off-chain for now; the on-chain cliffs and vesting of the release schedule are planned work. Within the validator share, the beacon committee receives the share of two shards, and each shard's committee splits the rest equally among its seated members. On a one-shard network this gives the beacon committee two thirds of the validator share. Changing that ratio is an open design question. Rewards accumulate per address and are claimed with a withdraw-reward transaction.
python3 tests/devnet/check.py verifies the split against these shares after the first epoch, and --stakers verifies that an outside validator is seated and paid.
